## Question
1. What integer value does `4 % 2` produce under the ECMAScript remainder operator, per spec?
2. What is the minimum Node.js version supporting the built-in `node:test` module used by this project's `test` script?

## Local context (verified)
This project's `package.json` defines:
```
"test": "node --test"
```
`node --test` invokes Node's built-in test runner, which is implemented by the `node:test` core module — so the relevant module to check is `node:test`.

## Sources
- [ECMAScript® 2027 Language Specification — § 12.9.3 Multiplicative Operators](https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-language-expressions.html#sec-multiplicative-operators) (defines the `%` operator via the `Number::remainder` abstract operation, § 6.1.6.1.6)
- [MDN — Remainder (%)](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Operators/Remainder) (cross-check; cites the same ECMA-262 spec section and gives `4 % 2 // 0` as the worked example)
- [Node.js v22.x — Test runner docs](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v22.x/api/test.html)
- [Node.js current (v26.x) — Test runner docs](https://nodejs.org/api/test.html) (History table: "Added in: v18.0.0, v16.17.0"; "The test runner is now stable" as of v20.0.0)

## Verified findings
- **`4 % 2` → `0`**. Per ECMA-262 § 12.9.3, the `%` operator on Numbers is computed by the `Number::remainder(n, d)` abstract operation. For finite, non-zero, evenly-divisible operands like 4 and 2, the result is the value `r` such that `4 = 2 × q + r` with `r` having the same sign as the dividend and `|r| < |d|`; since 4 is evenly divisible by 2, `r = 0`. MDN's documentation (which cites this same spec section) confirms this with the explicit example `4 % 2 // 0`.
- **Minimum Node.js version for `node:test`: v18.0.0**, with an additional backport to the v16.17.0 release line. This is stated verbatim in the "History" table at the top of the official Node.js Test runner documentation on both the v22.x archived docs and the current docs site. Note the module became **stable** (Stability 2) starting in **v20.0.0**; in v18.0.0/v16.17.0 it was present but not yet marked stable.

## Inference
- Because this project's `test` script (`node --test`) exercises the `node:test`-backed runner rather than importing `node:test` explicitly, the same minimum-version constraint (v18.0.0, or v16.17.0 on the 16.x line) applies to whatever Node.js binary runs `npm test` in this repo. This is a direct inference from the local `package.json`, not itself a claim requiring separate external sourcing.

## Unknowns / caveats
- I did not find an `.nvmrc`, `engines` field, or CI config in this fixture specifying a pinned/required Node.js version for the project — so I can't confirm whether the project enforces a version at or above v18.0.0 beyond what `node --test` itself requires at runtime.
- Version-sensitive caveat: on the v16.x line, `node:test` is only available from **v16.17.0** onward (not the whole v16 major); on v18.x it's available from **v18.0.0** (the whole major line, since it launched with the module included).
